newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says House vote on Mexico is "wrong".
newsitem.headline: Clinton says House vote on Mexico is "wrong".

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday criticised the House of Representatives vote to decertify Mexico for its efforts in the war against drugs, saying it was "the wrong way to protect the interests of the American people."

In a one-page statement issued by the travelling White House, Clinton stopped short of threatening to veto the congressional action, but said, "I will continue to work with Congress to ensure that legislation that would undermine progress we have made with Mexico does not become law."

"Today's vote by the House of Representatives on Mexico is the wrong way to continue and deepen the unprecedented cooperation we are getting from Mexico in the war on drugs -- and the wrong way to protect the interests of the American people," Clinton said in the statement.

Clinton praised anti-drug efforts by Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, and said, "He deserves our support -- not a vote of 'no confidence' that will only make it more difficult for him to work with us and defeat the scourge of drugs."

The House vote essentially overturns Clinton's certification that Mexico is an ally in the fight against drugs -- unless he reports within 90 days that Mexico has made substantial progress in improving its performance.
The resolution softens the blow to Mexico by waiving the economic sanctions that normally would result from such decertification.
